html:
After the failed Tibetan uprising of 1959, tens of thousands of Tibetans followed the 14th Dalai Lama over the Himalayas into exile in India, Nepal and Bhutan.

The crossing was hard: many died of cold, hunger and disease in the hot lowlands. India's prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru gave them asylum. Refugees first worked on road gangs in the mountains, then the Indian government gave land for farming settlements, the largest at Bylakuppe in the south. The Dalai Lama settled at Dharamshala, which became the seat of the Central Tibetan Administration, the government in exile.

The exiles rebuilt their great monasteries in India and set up schools to keep the Tibetan language and culture alive. Later generations spread to Europe and North America. The exile community became the main voice for Tibet in the world, while Tibetans inside China lived under ever tighter control.
sum: After the failed Tibetan uprising of 1959, tens of thousands of Tibetans followed the 14th Dalai Lama over the Himalayas into exile in India, Nepal and Bhutan.
